clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather's stroke in June 1991, within the year: your wrist injury stopped your playing that October, you and Rafe clashed and he moved out, you were getting high and absorbed in radios, your mother married Desmond that autumn, and by early 1992 you were lost and low with no footing. Your grandmother Winifred's thyroid surgery sits in these months too but carries no shifts of yours or your parents' around it, so it stays outside.

clusters.name: Your grandfather Clifford's return and your father's remarriage, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Clifford coming back into the family in early 1989, within five years: your family moved to Quarry Lane and then the rebuilt Hollin Road house that autumn, you took to late nights, you left off chess and debate for music, your sister Tara was born in July 1990, your mother filled in your college forms and you underfunctioned, and by early 1994 you were stung that your dad had never heard of the film you were making. You found your drive again that year with the exchange in Portugal, so the period settles then.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer diagnosis, 2001–2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer found in 2001 or 2002, within years: you were running out of steam for performing and anxious, a disastrous audition left you done with it, you were on poor terms with family and friends and left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, you met Marisol and moved to Fenwick, you split with her and sank into deep depression, you could not face your family and relied on friends instead, and you cut off from your mother when you left for nursing school that August. You stopped speaking to her for roughly a year. Your grandmother spent her final months in your parents' home in 2003, and she died of the cancer in February 2004, but the period is your own reaction to the years of loss and upheaval, not hers; every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within months: you were too drained for conversation with your mother while building at Alder Creek in July, she pressed you to visit and you kept the door shut on her, you left for nursing school and cut off from her, and your aunt Imogen had a stroke with months of rehabilitation in early 2009. The cutoff held for roughly a year once you moved to Marlow Sound that September.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within years: you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along, your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017, your sister Tara married and flies for a regional airline, your aunt Imogen's memory loss worsened and she lashed out when muddled, your job steadied and paid well by June 2019 so your anxiety dropped, but you felt you ought to be driving projects forward, you started a sleeping pill, you aimed for shorter regular calls with your mother, and that October at her mother's retirement party at the lake house Wren was swamped one thing after another, you overfunctioned laying out a plan to settle her, her family fused close in talk all day, she settled once the plan was in place, but you awoke from the small hours with no more sleep and could only pull back as the others rose, and she was anxious when he'd had no sleep at family occasions.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
